quiz.title: Module 2 — Professional Talking-Head Editing
quiz.description: Monday's quiz covers the talking-head editing tutorial: the app used, building the composition with masks and text, text duplication and animation, keyframes, background removal, and creating visual emphasis.

questions.prompt: In the tutorial, which editing application is used to create the professional talking-head video?
options: Adobe Photoshop
CapCut Mobile
PixelLab
Lightroom Mobile
questions.explanation: The whole course works on CapCut Mobile. Photoshop and PixelLab belong to the graphics design track, and Lightroom is for photo editing.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of adding a black background overlay and a horizontal mask during the editing process?
options: To remove all the text from the video
To increase the video's playback speed
To create a structured visual area for the text and composition
To convert the video into an audio file
questions.explanation: The mask carves out a defined area of the frame, so the text and visuals sit inside a deliberate composition instead of being scattered over the whole picture.

questions.prompt: Which text colour is used for the initial text elements in the tutorial?
options: White
Red
Green
Blue
questions.explanation: The editor starts with white text, because it reads clearly against the darkened background and gives the cleanest base to recolour later.

questions.prompt: Why does the editor duplicate text elements during the editing process?
options: To remove the original video footage
To create additional text elements with different words and styling
To reduce the video resolution
To replace all animations with static images
questions.explanation: Duplicating keeps the existing formatting and position, so the editor can spin out new words and styling from a working base instead of rebuilding each element from scratch.

questions.prompt: Which of the following animation combinations is used for different text elements in the tutorial?
options: Fade in and rotate only
Zoom in and spin only
Bounce and flash only
Slide right, slide left, slide up, and slide down
questions.explanation: The editor uses the slide presets, moving different text elements in from different directions so the composition builds rather than all arriving at once.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of using keyframes when working with images and other visual elements?
options: To automatically correct spelling mistakes
To control changes in an element's position, scale, or rotation over time
To permanently remove the background from every clip
To change the video's audio volume
questions.explanation: A keyframe marks a value at a point in time. Set two and the editor animates between them, which is how an element moves, grows or rotates across the timeline.

questions.prompt: Which technique does the editor use to remove the background from an image or visual element?
options: Chroma key or the remove-background feature
Text duplication
Horizontal alignment
Playback speed adjustment
questions.explanation: Chroma key or the remove-background tool strips the backdrop so the subject can sit directly on the composition, without a hard rectangle around it.

questions.prompt: Why does the editor apply different colours, font styles, glow effects, and animations to selected text elements?
options: To make every word appear identical
To reduce the number of elements in the timeline
To create visual emphasis and make the text composition more engaging
To eliminate the need for image overlays
questions.explanation: Variation directs the eye. Colour, weight, glow and animation separate what matters from what supports it, so the viewer knows where to look.
